title: Judge appears skeptical of Pentagon arguments in legal fight over Anthropic 'supply chain risk' designation
key_facts: US District Judge Rita Lin in San Francisco heard Anthropic's challenge to the Pentagon's designation of it as a 'supply chain risk' on Tuesday (29 Sep 2026 by the article's dating); the Trump administration had ordered agencies to stop using Anthropic's products.

Lin said the government's actions did not seem 'tailored to the stated national security concern' and that it 'looks like an attempt to cripple Anthropic', asking whether it was punished for criticising the government's contracting position in the press.
She did not rule and said she would decide the preliminary injunction motion within days.

Deputy Assistant Attorney General Eric Hamilton argued Anthropic might 'sabotage' the military through a future software update or 'kill switch', but could not say whether Anthropic can push such an update.
Hamilton said he knew of no authority letting the Defense Department bar contractors from using a company's products for non-Defense work, contradicting Secretary Hegseth's earlier social media post.
Anthropic's lawyer Michael Mongan called the designation one 'in search of a justification' under the Administrative Procedure Act and said it caused 'immediate, irreparable and ongoing harm'.
quote_evidence: The judge concluded the hearing without issuing a ruling, instead vowing to decide the motion for a preliminary injunction within the next few days.
"What is troubling to me about these reactions is that they don't really seem to be tailored to the stated national security concern," she said.
"I'm not aware of any authorities that would permit DOW to categorically bar contractors from using a company's products or services for non-DOW work," he said.
why_it_matters_hint: A federal judge signalled she may block the Pentagon's attempt to cut Anthropic out of government work as retaliation.
event_date: Hearing on Tuesday, 29 Sep 2026 by the article's dating
notes: ABC's own courtroom reporting. The article says 'Tuesday'; with publication dated 3 Oct 2026 that is 29 Sep, so the event is before today's window and the ruling is still pending.
